content.text:
I submitted **factor-when-justified** with 0.8 confidence. I used 27 of the 60 budget.

The test counts below are the number of examples the learner needed to reach criterion; lower means cheaper to learn.

**Phase 1: is it part-based?** I trained four tasks that together used every rule exactly once: L1-S1-M1, L2-S2-M2, L3-S3-M3 and L4-S4-M4. Every untrained task was then made only of rules the learner had seen. A part-based learner should have found all of them cheap, but the savings depended only on how similar each task was to a trained one:

| Task | Similarity to closest trained task | Before training | After phase 1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| L2-S1-M1 | 0.5 | 52, 51 | 47 |
| L3-S4-M2 | 0.625 | 36 | 33 |
| L1-S1-M2 | 0.75 | 24 | 11 |

That rules out part-based. A holistic learner and a factor-when-justified learner both fit this pattern, since no rule had appeared twice yet.

**Phase 2: holistic or factor-when-justified?** I trained six more tasks so that L2, S1 and M1 each appeared in three trained tasks. I picked them so that none was more than 0.5 similar to L2-S1-M1, which left that task's closest-match similarity unchanged.
- **L2-S1-M1** fell from about 50 to a median of about 24 (35, 20, 1, 8, 24, 42, 34). A holistic learner should not have changed, because the closest match didn't change.
- **L3-S4-M2** was the control, since its rules hadn't been repeated three times. It stayed at 33 and 33, with one stray reading of 1.

Rule recombination only started helping once the rules had been repeated, which is what factor-when-justified predicts.

**Caveats:**
- The test noise is large and includes occasional outliers (readings of 1). The 47 for L2-S1-M1 after phase 1 is a single sample, although it matches the two untrained readings of 51 and 52.
- A holistic learner that adds up similarity across all trained tasks, rather than using only the closest one, could explain some of the drop. The newly trained tasks were only weakly similar to L2-S1-M1, which makes that less likely, but I didn't test it directly.
- I didn't try to work out whether k is 2 or 3, since the verdict doesn't depend on it.
